summary: Hourly reserved capacity credit reversed unexpectedly after staggered metering window
description: Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected reversal of an auto-applied reserved-capacity credit that appeared as a negative credit line in their hourly billing export. The reversal shows up ~30-45 minutes after the hour boundary and then a corrected credit is applied two hours later. Impact: Customer is concerned this will cause invoice mismatches and reconciliation chaos for their finance team. They have 3 active dedicated pools (dev/prod/analytics) and observed the anomaly on the prod pool. Timeline and identifiers: - Customer org id: org_sparkline_01 - Affected pool: prod-gpu-pool-7 - Sample hour window: 2026-03-07T18:00:00Z - 2026-03-07T19:00:00Z - Billing export shard: hourly-usw2-2026-03-07-18 - Support ticket received via email at 2026-03-08T09:12Z.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs sustained production traffic against prod-gpu-pool-7 between 18:00-19:30 UTC.
2) Billing metering service produces hourly export at ~18:05 UTC for the 18:00 hour.
3) An auto-applied reserved-capacity credit is computed and attached as credit_2026-03-07-18 on the export.
4) At ~18:40 UTC a reversal transaction credit_rev_2026-03-07-18 appears for the same credit id, showing negative credit on the export.
5) At ~20:10 UTC the pipeline replays and writes credit_fix_2026-03-07-18 restoring the expected credit amount.
Observed result: temporary negative credit, later corrected; Customer wants explanation and assurance no duplicate charges will remain on the final invoice.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): confirmed export shows temporary negative credit and subsequent correction; customer CSV snapshot attached.

SRE note: observed a consumer lag event on kafka topic billing-metering-usw2 at 18:36 UTC. Consumer group billing-aggregator resumed and replayed offsets which caused a second write that looked like a reversal followed by a corrective write.

Billing-engineering hypothesis: reserved-capacity credit calculation runs in two stages across two micro-batches (allocation + finalization). If finalization batch is reprocessed out-of-order due to a lag/replay, a reversal record may be emitted and then later corrected when finalization completes.

Reproduction attempt: simulated a consumer group restart with overlapping replay in staging and reproduced mirrored temporary reversal lines in the hourly export. Root cause likely interaction between idempotency keys and late replay handling in the billing-aggregator (missing de-dup guard for credit finalization idempotency).

Potential scope: customers with dedicated hourly reservations in us-west region during the 2026-03-07 18:00-19:00 window. Early estimate: <40 orgs impacted but further sweep required via billing logs.
